facts.fact: CAN-SPAM is a U.S. law focused on regulating commercial email, not on governing every way a business collects or stores customer data.
facts.quote: CAN-SPAM is a U.S. law focused on commercial email. Its job is to regulate how a business sends promotional messages, not to govern every way that business collects or stores customer data.

facts.fact: GDPR can apply to lead forms, remarketing audiences, CRM entries, and follow-up campaigns when they involve data from EU residents.
facts.quote: A lead form, remarketing audience, CRM entry, and follow-up campaign can all fall in scope if they involve data from EU residents.

facts.fact: The page states that CAN-SPAM penalties can be assessed on a per-email basis.
facts.quote: CAN-SPAM can carry penalties on a per-email basis, as noted earlier.

facts.fact: The page states that GDPR relevance can arise when the data belongs to an EU resident, regardless of where the business is located.
facts.quote: If the data belongs to an EU resident, GDPR can become relevant.

facts.fact: The page recommends adding a valid physical postal address to every marketing email footer.
The page recommends that the unsubscribe option not require hunting through tiny text or logging into an account.
facts.quote: It should not require hunting through tiny text or logging into an account.

facts.fact: The page advises businesses not to keep unsubscribed contacts in a side spreadsheet for possible reactivation.
facts.quote: Do not keep unsubscribed contacts in a side spreadsheet for “possible reactivation.”

facts.fact: The page recommends using double opt-in when risk is higher, noting it adds friction but creates cleaner records and stronger proof.
facts.quote: Use double opt-in when risk is higher

facts.fact: The page advises businesses not to buy or scrape email lists and to build permission-based lists instead.
facts.quote: Do not buy lists. Do not scrape lists.
